reelection.rule: Rule: next even-year November for this House term. legislators-current.yaml ends the current term on 2027-01-03. The even-year November before that January 3 end is November 2026. The file has no election day, so no day of the month is shown.

said_voted.caption: Posts are shown as written. A post is matched to a vote only when it names the bill number or the bill's official title. A post can mention a bill for many reasons.

My team and I are aware of and are monitoring the horrific tragedy in the heart of Fairfield. I’m praying for the seven victims and their families, as well as the wider Fairfield community who are still struggling with this devastating situation.

I thank local and federal law enforcement for their swift response and service as they continue searching for the suspect. They have my full and unwavering support.

If you or someone you know has any information, please contact the Fairfield Police Department at 707-428-7600 or email 1030mall@fairfield.ca.gov or the Sacramento Field Office of the FBI at (916) 746-7000 or https://t.co/X7s74f2XaS

Patti and I are saddened by the news of Dolores Huerta’s passing.

Dolores was a very close personal friend and colleague with whom we worked for years on advancing social justice. We first worked with Dolores in 1976 during the farmworkers’ strike in San Joaquin County, where she bravely led the effort to improve working conditions for farmworkers.

Every moment of her extraordinary life was dedicated to improving the lives of working people.

Dolores’s determination to improve the conditions for working people brought her to Washington, D.C., where she and Patti marched hand-in-hand to improve the conditions for women.

Her work lives on through the Dolores Huerta Foundation and in the halls of Congress, where we will continue to work to make Dolores’s vision of workers’ rights a reality. I will never waver in my commitment to fighting for fair wages and safe, equitable working conditions for all workers.

Dolores also received the Presidential Medal of Freedom and coined the rallying cry “Sí se puede,” a phrase that will live on with her memory.

Dolores’s life and memory will forever be a reminder of what can be accomplished through grit, determination, and, most importantly, a love for justice for all.
